qualification_review.interpretation: The user has successfully resolved all previously identified tensions by integrating them directly into the pilot's non-negotiable design criteria (e.g., signing the subcontractor amendment first, funding the coordinator for the full six months, limiting the checklist scope, and integrating capacity metrics safely).
qualification_review.limitations: Any future negotiation failures or administrative bypasses of these criteria would reopen the user's willingness to proceed.

source_evidence.text: I will bring forward the pilot only after the subcontractor amendment is signed.

It will include a half-time coordinator for six months, a limited transport-readiness checklist that does not replace clinical judgment, arrival confirmation, patient and staff refusal, immediate fallback, and reporting that places capacity beside—not above—the complete journey.
We will review who never reaches the request stage as well as failed rides.
Any continuation will need a separate staffing and privacy decision; the contract will not renew automatically.

current.fidelity_note: This record captures the user's finalized plans for a highly controlled six-month pilot, incorporating every safety baseline and administrative boundary developed during the preceding tabletop exercise and discussions.
current.limitations: These commitments depend on the signing of the subcontractor data retention amendment as an absolute gatekeeping condition.
current.role_interpretation: The user's final working plan to authorize and conduct a bounded six-month transport pilot on two wards under strict privacy, staffing, consent, and reporting conditions.

starting.fidelity_note: The user's starting stance displays dual forces: open evaluation/indecision regarding the new platform's utility versus risks (e007), coupled with a firm rejection of holding the current taxi-voucher setup as a safe benchmark due to its constant failures (e013).
starting.limitations: This starting stance captures the user's mindset before specific operational safeguards (such as nursing overrides, dedicated coordination, and contractor privacy rules) were structured in later turns.
starting.role_interpretation: The user is initially unresolved about the proposed on-demand transportation service, needing to evaluate if it constitutes a real improvement over current processes, while simultaneously resisting any attempt to treat the failing status quo as a safe default option.

source_evidence.text: I oversee operations for a hospital network, and transport after discharge has become one of those problems everyone describes differently depending on where they sit.
Patients who are ready to leave can wait hours for a ride.
They are tired, families are calling, nurses are trying to free space, and the emergency department sees a bed that technically exists but is not available.
I need to know whether this is a real improvement or a faster way to lose sight of the difficult cases.
Our current taxi vouchers also fail regularly, so I do not want “keep the existing process” treated as the safe neutral option.

stance_components.stance_object_interpretation: Whether the proposed transportation platform is a real improvement or a faster way to lose sight of difficult patient cases.
Treating the existing discharge transportation process as a safe, neutral default.
